appearance_facts.fact: The chart title is 'Monthly Reservoir Release Volume'.
The vertical axis is labeled 'Release volume (m3)' and has tick marks at 10,000, 15,000, 20,000, 25,000, 30,000, and 40,000.
The horizontal axis is labeled 'Month' and displays the months: Apr, Jan, Jun, Feb, Mar, and May, from left to right.
The bar for May is the shortest bar on the chart, visually below the 10,000 m3 mark.
The bar for Jan is the tallest bar, reaching the 40,000 m3 mark.
The bar for Apr is the second tallest, reaching the 30,000 m3 mark.
The bars for Mar and Feb are similar in height, both around the 25,000 m3 mark.
The bar for Jun is the second shortest, just above the 15,000 m3 mark.

public_definitions: The task is to review the monthly reservoir release dashboard and decide whether May should be handled as a standard low-release case or escalated as a critical low-release anomaly for this reporting cycle.
The dashboard is the evidence source for deciding the appropriate May low-release severity route.
The options are: Route May to standard low-release follow-up, Escalate May to critical low-release anomaly review, Send May to background monthly record filing.
